known_limitation_finding.summary: Live-verified while building this fixture (2026-08-24): resolve_canonical_identity()'s title_author_year path is NOT robust to author-name-format variation. The SAME real paper, formatted as ['Luca D. Hargitai', ...] vs ['Hargitai, Luca D.'], produces two DIFFERENT identity keys -- because _first_author_surname() takes the raw first whitespace-split token after stripping commas, not a true parsed surname, so 'Luca' and 'Hargitai' are extracted from the two formats respectively.
known_limitation_finding.verification: Confirmed directly: resolve_canonical_identity({'title': 'Neurodiversity and mental health in adulthood', 'year': 2026, 'authors': ['Luca D. Hargitai', 'Lucy H. Waldren']}) and the same record with authors=['Hargitai, Luca D.'] produce different identity_key values.
known_limitation_finding.implication: This positive_group above deliberately uses IDENTICAL author-list formatting in both copies (the realistic case: the same extraction pipeline re-processing the same paper) -- it does not claim robustness to cross-provider name-format differences, which is a real, open gap for a future story to close, not something this fixture pretends is already solved.
